claims.text: Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems from provided demonstrations, representing aleatoric uncertainty.
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems from ambiguities tied to model configurations, representing epistemic uncertainty.
The proposed uncertainty estimation formulation operates in an unsupervised, plug-and-play fashion to quantify aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in in-context learning.

evidence.description: The authors identify provided demonstrations as the source of aleatoric uncertainty in LLM predictive uncertainty for in-context learning.
The authors identify model configuration ambiguities as the source of epistemic uncertainty in LLM predictive uncertainty for in-context learning.
The paper presents an unsupervised plug-and-play estimation method designed to decompose both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties.

methodologies.name: Unsupervised In-Context Learning Uncertainty Quantification
methodologies.description: An unsupervised, plug-and-play formulation and estimation method that decomposes predictive uncertainty in in-context learning into aleatoric (demonstrations) and epistemic (model configuration) uncertainties.

limitations.text: Existing uncertainty quantification works for LLMs often overlook the complex nature of LLMs and the uniqueness of in-context learning.
